newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia apparently to cut internal coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Colombia apparently to cut internal coffee price.

text.p: An unexpected announcement that Colombia was cutting its internal coffee price by 14,000 pesos per 125-kilo load as of next month sparked confusion and widespread voices of protest Thursday on the final day of an annual meeting of the National Coffee Growers' Congress.

The annoucement, which caught delegates to the meeting off guard, was made by the Congress' president, Carlos Alberto Gomez, after he held talks on the sidelines of the annual meeting with Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo and Jorge Cardenas, veteran leader of the National Coffee Growers' Federation.

Delegates shouted in protest as soon as Gomez read out the annoucement, saying they had not been consulted about the price cut during the previous three days of meetings at the Coffee Growers' Federation headquarters in Bogota.
It appeared to be official, however, and meant that the 235,500 pesos growers have been receiving for each 125-kilo load since Aug. 21 would be cut to 221,000 pesos with the start of the new year.
The price in effect since August was actually 221,500 pesos, but growers were awarded an additional 14,000 peso premium because of the poor outlook for this year's harvest.
The premium, which growers now look set to lose, was paid in the form of a bond instead of cash.

The cut announced by Gomez comes against the backdrop of a deepening financial crisis in the National Coffee Fund, an institution co-administered by the government and Grower's Federation that is used to pay growers for their coffee.
Cardenas warned Wednesday that the fund faces a yawning fiscal deficit and may not have enough money to buy Colombia's harvest in the 1997-98 coffee year.
